summary: Akiko Walley works in Japanology, history and archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Aoyama Gakuin University (~1994–2001) and Harvard University (~2001–2009), later holding a post at the University of Oregon (2009–2016).

Akimichi Eda is a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. from the University of Marburg (attested 2005) under doctoral supervisor Michael Hahn, and also studied under Katsumi Mimaki and Tsultrim Kelsang Khangkar.
Akio Donohashi specializes in Buddhist studies and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1976) and served as a professor at Kobe University (1990–1991).

Akio Minoura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts as an associate professor at Otani University (attested 2007–2013), as an overseas researcher at Stanford University (2012–2013), and with the Otani Academic Society.

Akio Tanabe is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1984–2006). He held posts at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1993), Kyoto University (1998, 2004), and the University of Tokyo (2015).

Akira Fujieda (1911–1998) worked in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and history/archaeology, having studied at Kyoto University (~1930–1934). He held posts at Kyoto University from 1937, becoming a professor in 1968, and held visiting professorships at Copenhagen and UC Berkeley.
Akira Hataya is a Buddhist studies scholar. He served as an associate professor at Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 1999) and as an emeritus professor at Otani University (attested 2014).

Akira Hirakawa (1915–2002) studied at the University of Tokyo under Shoson Miyamoto. A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1962–1975) and also held posts at Waseda University and ICPBS.

Akira Miyaji specializes in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Nagoya University (~1964–1991) and later held academic posts at Hirosaki University, Nagoya University, Ryukoku University, and the Ryukoku Museum.
Akira Momiyama works in Sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at Kyoto University (~1972–1976) and served as a professor at Saitama University (attested 2005).

Akira Mukai is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Hokkaido University, where he was an assistant (~1974), and later served as a professor at Hokkaido Musashi Women's Junior College (attested 1999).

Akira Omine (1929–2018) was a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Kyoto University under Kyoshi Takahama and at Heidelberg University, later holding professorships at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Osaka University, and Ryukoku University.

Akira Sadakata works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Hajime Nakamura, as well as the University of Paris, and served as an associate professor, professor, and professor emeritus at Tokai University.

Akira Saito specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Jikido Takasaki and earned his PhD at the Australian National University, later holding professorships at the University of Tokyo and ICPBS.

Akira Shimada is a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at the College of Art, Delhi, under Rajeev Lochan and Daud Ali, and has held positions at the British Museum and the State University of New York.

Akira Suganuma (1934–2016) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed doctoral studies at Toyo University (~1957–1962), where he later served as an assistant and associate professor, and taught at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies.

Akira Takeda (1930–2021) specialized in Sinology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Takeshiro Kuraishi, subsequently serving as a professor at the University of Tokyo (1965–1991) and teaching at Tokyo Woman's Christian University and Meikai University.
Akira Yamada (1922–2008) was a philosophy scholar. He studied at Kyoto University (~1943–1947) under Tokuryu Yamauchi and later held a post at Nanzan University (~1986–1993).

Akira Yuyama (1932–2021) worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and linguistics. He studied under Akira Hirakawa, Naoshiro Tsuji, Jan Willem de Jong, and Arthur Llewellyn Basham, and held positions at ANU, the International Institute for Buddhist Studies, and Soka University.

Akitoshi Saito works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He held posts as a professor (attested 1982) and emeritus professor (attested 2014) at Taisho University, and served as an adviser at the Kawasaki Daishi Research Institute.
